build.speed object keyed by movement mode; land required, others optional non-null integers. Scalar speed converts to {land}.
build.skills list with stable id = local skill id: pc_build stores proficiency rank, authored_statblock stores modifier. Unknown skill ids block.

rows.concept: actor state held at the campaign instance

observed.actor_row: Campaign-instance rows (campaign_id>0, 675 rows) carry per-campaign state in three forms: character_data (+ default_character_data merged at read), state_data, and hot columns hp_current/hp_max/armor_class/experience_points/position_q/position_r/position_h3/last_room_id/location_type/location_ref/facing/lifecycle_state/status.
observed.instance_state_data_keys: role, stats, description, content_id, backstory, basicInfo, inventory, resources, psychology, bonds, fears, equipment, motivations, runtime_entity_id, campaign_character_id, senses, skills, abilities, goals, attacks, quests, npc_profile, spells, defenses, actions, features, conditions, ...
observed.runtime_table: dc_campaign_actor_runtime_state (1758 rows, 368 campaigns) entity_payload.state repeats character_data (638), inventory, equipment, resources, currency, conditions, hit_points, spell_slots, focus_points, is_defeated; entity_payload.placement holds room_id, hex, facing, h3_index_res14.
observed.reader: CharacterStateService::getState() reads HP and AC from the instance row hot columns (CharacterStateService.php:147-158), overlays the campaign row state_data (:205), and merges default_character_data under character_data through alias chains. Its persistence path writes state_data and the hot columns together (:1699-1790). The coordinator separately persists dc_campaign_actor_runtime_state through ActorRuntimeMutationService. So the instance row is today's effective home for sheet state, and the runtime table is a second instance-level store.

rows.target_rule: Board directive: per-campaign actor state belongs to the campaign instance of the actor. The instance is the aggregate for its own state; a template never holds it and a template edit never resets it. Each instance fact still has exactly one physical home. Recommendation: instance row character_data = pinned authored snapshot; instance-scoped mutable facts (current HP, resources, expended slots, defeated/flags, XP, campaign role) = one typed instance-state document; placement = one placement record; inventory/effects/psychology keep their domain stores keyed by the instance. Hot columns and the duplicate copies become projections or are removed.
rows.blocks: S1 freeze of instance-scoped fields and all of S4. Requires the measured per-field map of which store wins today (instance row state_data vs hot columns vs runtime payload) before choosing each physical home.
rows.data_impact: Authored facts (description, backstory, abilities, attacks) are duplicated into instance state_data and again into runtime payload state.character_data; divergence between the copies has not been measured yet.

observed.reader: getState() resolves name as basicInfo.name ?? display_name ?? name ?? row.name, level as basicInfo.level ?? level ?? row.level, and similar chains for ancestry, class, background, appearance, saves.

rows.target_rule: One path per fact in the canonical document. Readers take that path or fail with a typed contract error; no alias chain, no default-under-override merge at read time.
